question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed grouped Claw lifecycle in core, including package-declared workspace instructions and durable per-file ownership records?
rationale: The implementation can be reviewed for correctness, but automation cannot decide whether this new packaging, persistence, consent, and trust model should become an OpenClaw product contract while its RFC remains open.

options.title: Hold for RFC acceptance
options.body: Keep this stack open but unlanded until maintainers approve or narrow the lifecycle and security model in the RFC.

options.title: Sponsor the current model
options.body: Confirm the grouped lifecycle direction and review the entire ordered stack as one compatibility and security-sensitive feature.

options.title: Reject the core feature
options.body: Close the stack if maintainers prefer existing manual workspace and plugin surfaces over a new core Claw lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Hold for RFC acceptance
recommendation.body: Keep this stack open but unlanded until maintainers approve or narrow the lifecycle and security model in the RFC.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision affects the core shared-state architecture and durable product contract that their current-main work introduced.
